title: 1995 Granada–Dakar Rally
who: Won by Pierre Lartigue / Michel Perin (Citroën) and Stéphane Peterhansel (Yamaha)
summary: The 1995 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 14 stage towns and bivouacs through Spain, Morocco, Mauritania, Senegal, Guinea. Winners — Cars: Pierre Lartigue / Michel Perin (Citroën); Bikes: Stéphane Peterhansel (Yamaha); Trucks: Karel Loprais / Radomír Stachura / Josef Kalina (Tatra 815).

sources.label: ESPN Deportes: Dakar winners through the years

approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.name: Motril
stops.text: The first Dakar to start outside France: stage 1 left Granada and ran 275 km, 170 km of it timed, down to the coast here before the crossing to Morocco.

stops.name: Errachidia
stops.text: Stage 2 from Nador: 619 km to the edge of the Sahara.

stops.name: Ouarzazate
stops.text: Stage 3: 574 km over the Atlas, 405 km of it timed.

stops.name: Guelmim
stops.text: Stage 4: 646 km to the gateway of the Sahara.

stops.name: Smara
stops.text: Stage 5 into Western Sahara, 408 km timed.

stops.name: Aousserd
stops.text: Stage 6: 577 km of special stage, almost all of the day.

stops.name: Zouérat
stops.text: Stage 7: 625 km timed into Mauritania, then a rest day.

stops.name: Chinguetti
stops.text: Stage 8: 504 km timed to the old caravan town of Chinguetti.

stops.name: Tidjikja
stops.text: Stage 9: 347 km timed across the Mauritanian desert.

stops.name: Ayoun El Atrous
stops.text: Stage 10: 375 km timed to the south of Mauritania.

stops.name: Labe
stops.text: Stage 12: 626 km timed into the hills of Guinea.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The finish. Pierre Lartigue and Michel Périn won the cars in a Citroën ZX, Stéphane Peterhansel his fourth bike title on a Yamaha, and Karel Loprais the trucks in a Tatra.
